display.title: Mitzvah Time: The Mezuzah, Welcoming Hashem Into Our Home
display.summary_short: Where the mezuzah goes, what it tells us, and the two places in Chumash Devarim where Hashem commands this mitzvah.
display.summary_long: A Mitzvah Time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains that a mezuzah is placed on the right doorpost as we enter a room, and that it is a sign that Hashem is welcome in our home and that the house and everyone in it belong to Hashem. The mitzvah is so important that the Torah writes it twice, in Chumash Devarim chapter 6 and chapter 11. Chapter 6 is the Shema, which every Jew says morning and night. Although on the radio the children say only the first twelve words, the Shema has three parts, beginning 'Shema Yisroel', 'Vehayah im shamoa' and 'Vayomer'. Listeners are asked to remember these facts for the call-in quiz.
display.lesson: A mezuzah on the door shows that Hashem is welcome in our home and that everything in it belongs to Him.

sources_cited.note: The mitzvah of mezuzah is written twice.
